newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Moody's assigns ratings to Pusan Bank.
newsitem.headline: Moody's assigns ratings to Pusan Bank.

text.p: Moody's Investors Services said on Thursday it had assigned the following first-time ratings to South Korea's Pusan Bank -
Pusan Bank, based in Pusan, Korea's largest port and second-largest city, had consolidated total assets of 12.66 trillion at end-December 1995.

Moody's said the ratings were based on the uncertainties in Pusan's local market during the slowdown in Korea's economy, and its vulnerability to the deteriorating conditions in the banking sector as seen by its rather weak financial performance lately.
But the bank's deposit ratings were supported by the probability of some regulatory assistance, if needed, based on its size and importance to a major industrial region.
Moody's noted Pusan's asset quality reflected the problems of local industries as the region shifted from textiles to other sectors such as automobiles, and its capital levels were thin.
Unemployement in the region was high and local bankruptcies rising, but the outlook may improve if investment plans of the government and industrial groups bore fruit, it said.
In line with most regional banks, Pusan's core profitability was quite strong although net income had been reduced by the deed for provisions for losses on loans and investments.
The bank was expanding domestically and internationally, and it had strengthened its trust business with new products.
